newsitem.title: USA: Arco Chemical says Q2 earnings unacceptable.
newsitem.headline: Arco Chemical says Q2 earnings unacceptable.

text.p: ARCO Chemical Co's slide in second quarter net income to $35 million, $0.36 per share, from $48 million, or $0.50 per share, in the first quarter and $81 million, or $0.84 per share a year ago is "disappointing" and "unacceptable", chief executive Alan Hirsig said in a statement.
"Compared to first quarter 1997, the second quarter reflects higher costs associated with three scheduled plant turnarounds," Hirsig said.

Turnaround costs in the second quarter were $23 million compared with $2.0 million in the first quarter and ARCO Chemical anticipates turnaround costs will be $10 million in the third quarter of 1997 and $13 million in the fourth quarter of 1997.
These costs were $16 million higher than a year ago.
The company has said it is to implement a cost reduction program which will save it $150 million a year out of annual expenses of $750 million and will shed 800-1,100 posts.
It will take a yet to be quantified charge this year for the program.

The company said that higher volumes of propylene oxide and butanediol contributed positively to earnings but that compressed product margins, resulting from higher costs for most raw materials and weaker product prices and the expiry of a number of fixed fee fuel additive MTBE contracts.
Revenue for the second quarter slid to $956 million compared with $1,029 million in the first quarter and $959 million a year ago.
The company is a quoted subsidiary of ARCO.
